speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for that information. To better understand your condition, have you noticed any changes in your skin, such as jaundice or itching, or any recent fevers? 

Also, could you describe the texture of the enlarged lymph node—is it hard, rubbery, or soft?

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling very tired and have had worsening abdominal pain for about four weeks. I have also had drenching night sweats and lost about twelve pounds.

speaker: Doctor
text: I'm glad you shared those details; the significant weight loss and drenching night sweats are very concerning. To narrow down the cause, have you experienced any recent fevers, or have you noticed any changes in your bowel habits like constipation, diarrhea, or blood in your stool? Also, do you have a history of smoking or alcohol use?

speaker: Patient
text: I noticed swelling in my neck over the last few days. It does not hurt, but it feels enlarged and fixed.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Hodgkin Lymphoma. The combination of painless, fixed supraclavicular lymphadenopathy, B-symptoms (fevers, night sweats, weight loss), and abdominal pain is highly suggestive of this malignancy. I am requesting a CT scan of the chest, abdomen, and pelvis, and a biopsy of the lymph node.
